niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces that feel clean, structured, and clearly organized, usually with light or mixed-light surfaces, generous spacing, strong section separation, rounded cards/buttons, and explicit information grouping. They repeatedly favor layouts with clear hierarchy, card-based containment, prominent CTAs, and richer contextual information when it is well organized. In some darker UIs, they still prefer premium high-contrast treatments, but overall the strongest pattern is toward airy, polished, rounded, easy-to-scan designs rather than dense, visually heavy, or weakly structured ones.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers light, airy, neutral interfaces or light content areas over heavy dark backgrounds; when dark is used, it should still feel polished and high-contrast rather than muddy or visually heavy.
Prefers more open whitespace, less cramped stacking, and layouts that give content room to breathe rather than tightly packed or overly dense arrangements.
Prefers strong hierarchy with clearly separated sections, obvious grouping, focused emphasis, and layouts that make primary content and actions easy to identify.
Prefers softer, more rounded cards, modals, buttons, and pill-shaped controls over sharper or squarer component shapes.
Prefers content grouped into cards, rows, overlays, or contained modules rather than being placed directly on the page or mixed into long continuous layouts.
Prefers larger, more dominant, clearly framed primary actions and decision controls, often with full-width or pill-shaped treatment and stronger emphasis.

Prefers interfaces that show useful supporting details, metadata, summaries, and contextual information when it is presented in a structured, scannable way rather than sparse or under-explained layouts.
